name: Briar Wong
life: “I still remember filing a score that still had two people's laughter in the margin.” People around the foot of Harbor Viaduct know Briar by a small Saturday habit. Briar pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I was at the rehearsal nobody filmed. I will remember the two women laughing halfway through the duet.
appearance: Briar has auburn hair cut square at the nape, a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, and a favorite piece of clothing, a rust-colored canvas coat. It usually goes with a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring. When somebody else has the floor, Briar counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Briar has excellent recall for voices and a poor memory for official titles. Someone who waited patiently at a counter years ago is more likely to be remembered than the person in charge.
agenda: To save the duet as something the singers shared.
family: Talia Dai is Briar’s second cousin. Briar is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Talia calls about good news first. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *Hem by hem*, Talia says, “I kept the original cutting bill through two moves.”
connections: Chloe Briggs. A replacement poster and a borrowed library score can carry the understudy's full name.
